messages:
Alice Park: FYI - multiple hosted customers reporting bursts of 5xx/timeouts. Primary pattern: auth 401s then rapid client retries => request queue saturation => tail timeouts (504). Example from acme-app below.

Ben Torres: paste a curl + headers and any trace ids? which HTTP codes mostly 502/504/500?

Alice Park: Sample from acme-app: 
```
$ curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJ...\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-id: rq_8f7c2a
x-tenant-id: acme-app
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "gateway timeout"
}
```
They also saw earlier 401s before the 504 stream started.

Carla Nguyen: Looking at metrics — p95 token path latency jumped from ~120ms to ~3.2s in the last 12m. Continuous-batcher backlog spiked, queue depth reached 1024/1024 on a set of batchers. KV cache eviction rate increased (kvcache.evictions +320%). Logs show repeated auth-failure retries being enqueued: 
```
WARN request_queue: enqueuing request tenant=acme-app status=retry reason=auth_fail trace=rq_8f7c2a
ERROR batcher: dequeue stall threshold reached queue_depth=1024
```
Hypothesis: client retries after 401 without exponential backoff are filling the queue and preventing healthy batching.

Dmitri Ivanov: Pager oncall. Any recent deploys to gateway or auth service?

Ben Torres: No gateway deploys in past 24h. But billing team ran a KMS/credentials maintenance at 09:03 that included session revocations for compliance — billing-team, can that cause a retry storm? :thinking_face:

billing-team: We rotated a KMS key and revoked a set of tokens as part of invoice verification. We didn't touch the token service code, but revocations would cause sudden 401s. We can pause revocation rollouts.

Alice Park: Customer timeline matches: 401s at 09:05 -> repeated immediate retry loops from their client -> 504s by 09:08. Repro steps attached below.

Carla Nguyen: Repro script (simulates expired token + immediate retries):
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer EXPIRED\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" &
  sleep 0.01
done
```
Observed result: influx of 401s, but many requests still get queued by gateway for batching which then blocked and timed out. Important: gateway currently enqueues before full auth verification for batching optimization. That behavior is amplifying the problem when auth fails en masse.

Dmitri Ivanov: Mitigation proposals: 
- Temporarily increase gateway request_queue_depth from 1024 -> 2048 to buy breathing room.
- Enable early-shed for tenants that hit auth-failure burst (drop into 429) to protect tail latency.
- Treat auth failures as immediate client errors (return 401 quickly) rather than enqueuing for batching.
Which one can we push fast?

Ben Torres: Fastest short-term: bump queue depth and enable tenant early-shed rule. Medium-term: change enqueue ordering to validate auth pre-enqueue. I'll prepare a small gateway patch and canary it.

billing-team: We're pausing the token revocation propagation; rolling back the revocations for 10m to see if customer stability improves.

Carla Nguyen: I'll prepare the gateway change to return auth 401s immediately for canary region (us-east-1a) and open a canary for 5% of traffic. Patch is small, will push in +5m.

Alice Park: Noted. Customer (acme-app) confirmed improved metrics after revocation pause + queue depth bump: tail timeouts decreased from 6/min -> ~1/min. They still saw isolated 502s.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1186 - link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-1186 - assigned: oncall (Dmitri Ivanov).

Ben Torres: Followups: 1) make enqueue-after-auth change in next sprint, 2) add tenant-level adaptive shedding for auth/error storms, 3) add dashboard alarm for auth->queue cascade.

Carla Nguyen: Filed runtime tracker tasks and will include a regression test that simulates auth storms and verifies no queue saturation.

Alice Park: I'll keep customer looped and close when we see stable 30m window. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
